description: Figure 2 is a concentric pie chart, also known as a donut chart, illustrating a hierarchical taxonomy of medical ethics. The inner circle is divided into four large, distinct colored segments, each representing one of the four pillar principles of medical ethics: Beneficence (blue), Non-Maleficence (purple), Autonomy (green), and Justice (orange). The outer circle, which surrounds the inner one, is segmented into 26 smaller, colored wedges, each corresponding to a specific category derived from a larger set of 256 detailed principles. These 26 categories are visually grouped and radiate outward from their respective pillar principle in the inner circle, with each wedge labeled with its specific ethical category (e.g., “Provide Medical Care to Patients,” “Respect Life, Dignity of Patients,” “Prevent Patient from Harm,” “Maintain Confidential”). The chart uses color-coding to link the outer categories to their parent pillar, creating a clear visual representation of the taxonomy’s structure. The caption confirms that the inner circle contains the four pillars and the outer circle contains the 26 clustered categories.
